tasks.title: Make the site's size budget stop the build, not just print a line
tasks.why: publish.py:32-34 prints 'the site is over its budget... Prune img/ by hand, or lower PER_ASSET' when the built site passes MAX_FILES/MAX_BYTES, but sync() still returns normally and build.py:132 never checks it or publish.py's exit code. ops.py --watch runs build.py headless and unattended, so the print lands in a log nobody reads; main() exits 0 regardless. The check that was meant to catch a harvest filling the Drive cannot fail, so it never prompts the one by-hand step (pruning img/, or lowering PER_ASSET in src_images.py:18) it names as the fix, and the Drive can keep growing past 400 MB unnoticed.
tasks.done_when: build.py exits non-zero (or writes a warning file ops.py's page surfaces) when publish.sync finds the site over MAX_FILES/MAX_BYTES, and a test fixture that forces the over-budget branch asserts that signal.
